evidence: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:70 has the comment '// cannot use @BeforeAll, realm is not initializaed yet'. The typo is real. It is only in a test comment, so it has no functional impact.

GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:300 is a line with only 8 spaces (diff line '+        '). It sits between createGroupPermission(...) and the '//create new user' comment and leaves a stray double blank line. This is a cosmetic formatting nit.

GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:2 says 'Copyright 2024', while the new GroupPermissionsV2.java:2 says 'Copyright 2025'. Sibling files in the same fgap test package mix both years: AbstractPermissionTest, PermissionRESTTest and UserResourceTypePermissionTest use 2024, while FeatureDisabledTest and FeatureV1EnabledTest use 2025. The package follows no single convention, and the year in the header has no functional effect.

GroupPermissionsV2.java:70: canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). hasPermission (lines 151-160) returns true if ANY granted scope matches, so a VIEW-only permission on all groups grants canManage(). The per-group canManage(GroupModel) at line 79 correctly checks only MANAGE, and V1 GroupPermissions.java:274-275 only allows MANAGE_USERS. Real impact: GroupsResource.java:181 addTopLevelGroup calls auth.groups().requireManage(). An admin with only the 'view' scope on the Groups resource type could therefore create top-level groups and move groups to top level. This is a privilege escalation. Fix: change line 70 to hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE).

GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:68 reads 'private final GroupRepresentation topGroup = new GroupRepresentation();;'. The double semicolon is real. It is a legal empty declaration and harmless, but it is sloppy and should be cleaned up.
